guestStories.subtitle: See what visitors say about their experience
guestStories.testimonial: An unforgettable experience. The alpacas were wonderful, the guides were knowledgeable and warm, and the whole farm exuded peace and authenticity.

reviews.sue: I visited at the end of August and had a fantastic time! Ibiza has so much to offer in addition to the music and I would highly recommend a visit to see the beautiful Alpacas. You can feed them and learn so much about these amazing animals ❤️. I was warmly welcomed and had such a valuable experience. Go and see them - you'll love it and them!
reviews.verena: We visited the sweet, fluffy alpacas. A super nice couple guides you through the alpaca enclosures with great information about these animals. You have the opportunity to feed, pet, and even give an alpaca kiss. The animals are very trusting and are thrilled by your closeness and food. It was a wonderful experience and I can only recommend it to everyone who is in Ibiza. 🤗🥳
reviews.gemma: I made a group booking for 6 of us for Friday 9th May. Bart got in touch to let me know that they were actually closed that day because they were shearing the Alpacas. He then kindly offered to accommodate us the day before even though the farm was closed, it was really kind of him to do so. The experience itself was amazing. Bart was so knowledgeable and friendly and the Alpacas were so sweet. All the Alpacas are very well cared for and adore Bart which shows how much he loves them.
reviews.renate: Really fun to do with our 2 boys aged 12, but actually fun for all ages. We actually knew nothing about Alpacas, it was very interesting! It took exactly one hour.
reviews.sven: Highly recommended! Bart & San run a fantastic operation. The ultimate Chill Out experience 🦙❤️🦙
reviews.paul: Went September 23, amazing tour, Bart is so knowledgeable and friendly. If you have a car it's a must 😀🦙

faq.sectionSubtitle: Everything you need to know before your visit

duration.q: How long is a typical tour?
duration.a: Standard tours are 2–3 hours. Workshops and extended experiences can be customized. We recommend checking available time slots when booking.

languages.a: We offer tours in English, Spanish, and Dutch. If you need another language, please contact us.

children.a: Yes! Tours are family-friendly. Children should be supervised, especially around the animals. We recommend ages 4+, but younger children can come with parental guidance.

wear.a: Wear comfortable, closed-toe shoes suitable for farm terrain. Bring sun protection in summer. Light layers are ideal, as the farm is outside. Avoid loud colors or strong perfumes to keep alpacas calm.

accessibility.q: Is the farm accessible for people with disabilities?
accessibility.a: Our farm is on natural terrain. Please contact us ahead to discuss accessibility and how we can accommodate your needs.

food.q: Can we bring food or drinks?
food.a: Outside food is not permitted, but we offer organic refreshments. We accommodate dietary restrictions—mention this when booking.

booking.q: How do I book a tour?
booking.a: Use our online booking system below to check availability and reserve your spot. Group bookings and custom experiences: contact us for options.

cancellation.q: What if I need to cancel or reschedule?
cancellation.a: Cancellations up to 48 hours before your tour receive a full refund or rebooking. Less notice incurs a 50% fee.

private.q: Do you offer private tours or group events?
private.a: Yes! We offer private farm experiences, weddings, corporate retreats, and alpaca yoga sessions. Contact us for custom packages.

parking.a: Yes, free parking is available on-site. Spots are limited—arrive 15 minutes early to allow parking time.

alcacaPage.title: Alcaca Oro Negro
alcacaPage.metaTitle: Alcaca Oro Negro | Alpaca Manure Fertilizer – Alpacas Ibiza
alcacaPage.metaDescription: Alcaca Oro Negro is natural alpaca-manure fertilizer from Es Currals, Ibiza. Called "black gold" in the Andes — odorless, ready-to-use, available from 125 g mini-bags to bulk orders.
alcacaPage.subtitle: Black gold from the Andes — the purest, most fertile natural fertilizer, made on Es Currals from our own herd.
alcacaPage.storyBody: In Peru, alpaca manure has been prized for centuries under the name "Oro Negro" — black gold. Alpacas are pseudo-ruminants with three stomach chambers; their 65-hour digestion produces the purest and most fertile manure of all animal species, in the form of small, odorless black pellets. Alcaca Oro Negro is made on Es Currals from the manure of our own herd. Bart manually designed and built a filter system to remove stones, weeds, and sand. The result: ready-to-use fertilizer that needs no composting, attracts no flies or insects, and can even be used indoors. It works optimally for months to years and is available from 125 g mini-bags to hundreds of kilograms.
alcacaPage.photo1Alt: Alcaca Oro Negro — alpaca manure fertilizer bags
alcacaPage.photo2Alt: Alcaca Oro Negro — close-up of the product
alcacaPage.benefit1: The purest, most fertile manure of all animal species — small odorless black pellets
alcacaPage.benefit2: Ready-to-use from the bag: no composting needed, no flies, no unpleasant smell
alcacaPage.benefit3: Works optimally for months to years on vegetables, flowers, herbs, and trees
alcacaPage.benefit4: Manually filtered at Es Currals — stones, weeds, and sand removed by hand

about.title: About Alpacas Ibiza
about.metaTitle: About Alpacas Ibiza | Es Currals Farm – Bart & San
about.storyText: Es Currals Alpacas Ibiza is the dream made real of Belgian couple San and Bart. Years ago San's weaving passion brought them into contact with alpacas and their remarkable wool — and from that moment two dreams grew together: a farm of their own, and a move to the paradise island of Ibiza. On 10 August 2019, after years of research and months of hard work making their finca alpaca-ready, five beautiful alpacas arrived in the early morning hours from Belgium: Mojo, Lewis, Marrón, Dusty and Barbarella. They found their new home — Es Currals Alpacas Ibiza — on a traditional Ibicenco finca amid the wild nature of northern Ibiza. The farm was welcomed from the start by Maria, an 81-year-old local Ibizan woman whose family had kept livestock on the land for generations. The name Es Currals is taken from the Catalan word for the stone animal enclosures found on historic Ibizan farms — a tribute to Maria and to the northern Ibiza community. Since then the herd has grown to fourteen: stud Lewis fathered three island-born cria (Chet, Toots and Bardot), and six more arrived in spring 2021 from Belgian breeder Alpaca Flanders. OWNER_REVIEW_TRANSLATION
about.weavingSubtitle: Made in Ibiza, embracing the world
about.weavingDescription: San caught the weaving bug in 2013. She started with small table looms, then invested in a traditional Swedish wooden loom from a 92-year-old master weaver who gave her private lessons — she kept the loom's original name: Big Ben. Every step from shearing to finished cloth is done by hand at Es Currals. San hand-washes and hand-cards the fleece, spins the yarn, and colours it with natural plant extracts — hibiscus, avocado, and other flowers. She weaves on Big Ben using centuries-old patterns from historical manuscripts, blended with contemporary fashion. Every Wishfulfilling Weaving creation is a unique, non-duplicable work of art, made to order. OWNER_REVIEW_TRANSLATION

adopt.title: Adopt an Alpaca
adopt.subtitle: Support Ibiza's first alpaca farm and become part of the Es Currals herd. Choose monthly or yearly — your support keeps the farm thriving.
adopt.yearlyTierTagline: Same total as monthly, paid upfront — no recurring charges
adopt.benefitsIntro: Every adoption supports the herd and gives you a year of perks — from free farm visits to handcrafted goods from our weavers.
adopt.benefit1: Adoption certificate with your sponsored alpaca's name
adopt.benefit2: Six free farm tours per year (up to 4 guests each)
adopt.benefit3: 5 kg of Alcaca natural alpaca-fibre fertilizer shipped each season
adopt.benefit4: Welcome gift bundle: calendar, planner, keychain, framed photo
adopt.benefit5: Professional photoshoot session with your alpaca
adopt.benefit7: 15% discount on the Alpacas Ibiza Farm Shop
adopt.pickerSubheading: Choose a specific alpaca to support, or let us match you with one of the herd.
adopt.ctaSubtext: Secure checkout via Mollie. You'll receive a welcome email and adoption certificate within a few days.
adopt.faqSubtitle: Quick answers to the questions adopters ask most.
adopt.faqQ1: How long does the adoption last?
adopt.faqA1: One full year from the day of payment. Your perks (free tours, photoshoot, fertilizer shipments) are valid across that whole year.
adopt.faqQ2: Can I cancel a monthly adoption?
adopt.faqA2: Yes, any time. Use the subscription portal at the bottom of this page to cancel — you keep access to the year's perks already used. Yearly adoptions are paid upfront and non-refundable, but you keep all the benefits.
adopt.faqQ3: Can I visit my adopted alpaca?
adopt.faqA3: Absolutely — that's the point. Your adoption includes 6 free farm tours per year (up to 4 guests each visit). You'll meet your alpaca and the rest of the herd.
adopt.faqQ4: What if I pick a specific alpaca?
adopt.faqA4: Your certificate names that alpaca and your welcome email mentions them. If you pick "Pick for me", we'll match you with one of the herd and let you know within a few days.
adopt.faqQ5: Do you ship the fertilizer internationally?
adopt.faqA5: Inside Spain, yes — included in the price. For other EU countries, we cover shipping up to a reasonable cost; outside the EU we ask for help with postage. Get in touch before adopting if shipping is a concern.
adopt.faqA6: You can adopt on behalf of someone else — at checkout, enter their name and email. They'll get the welcome email and certificate. Contact us first if you'd like to time the welcome around a birthday or holiday.
adopt.faqQ7: What payment methods do you accept?
adopt.faqA7: Major cards (Visa, Mastercard, Amex), Apple Pay, Google Pay, iDEAL, Bancontact, and SEPA Direct Debit. All processed via Mollie — we never see your card or account details.

yoga.title: Alpaca Yoga
yoga.subtitle: Hatha yoga among the alpacas — 1 hour 15 minutes, max 6 guests. Every Wednesday and Saturday.
yoga.whatBody: A 75-minute outdoor Hatha yoga session held in the alpaca paddock at Es Currals finca in the rural north of Ibiza. Practise surrounded by the gentle presence of our herd — they graze freely around you while your guide leads the session.
yoga.whyBody: Alpacas are naturally calming animals. Their unhurried pace, soft sounds, and curious nature create an environment that deepens relaxation and focus. Guests consistently report that the presence of the herd makes it easier to stay present on the mat.
yoga.whenBody: Sessions run every Wednesday and Saturday. The yoga area is on the finca in San Carlos, rural north Ibiza. Contact us to confirm the start time for your preferred date, and for off-season availability.
yoga.priceBody: €30 per person. Maximum 6 participants per session to keep the experience intimate and to respect the alpacas' space.
yoga.scheduleNote: Wednesday & Saturday sessions. Contact us for the current start time and seasonal availability.

audience.a: No experience is necessary. The session is suitable for all levels, including complete beginners. The instructor adapts to the group.

bring.a: Comfortable clothing you can move in, and sunscreen for outdoor sessions. Contact us to confirm whether mats are provided or if you should bring your own.

weather.a: Sessions may be rescheduled or moved to a sheltered area in poor weather. We will contact you in advance if conditions require a change.

refund.a: Cancellations made at least 48 hours in advance receive a full refund or rebooking. Later cancellations may incur a 50% fee.

weddings.welfareText: Our alpacas are socialized, calm, and accustomed to guests. All appearances are supervised by an experienced handler. We only accept bookings we are confident are safe and comfortable for the herd.

welfare.gentleDesc: Our herd is used to people and calm in new settings.

weddings.bookingText: Whether you are hosting at our finca or need us to bring the alpacas to your venue, we will work with you to create the right experience. Get in touch to start planning.

notice.q: How far in advance should I book?
notice.a: We recommend booking as early as possible — at least 4–6 weeks ahead for standard shoots and as far in advance as possible for weddings. Popular dates fill quickly in peak season (May–October).

location.q: Can you bring alpacas to our venue?
location.a: Yes, off-site appearances are available. Contact us with your venue location and we will confirm whether it is within our travel area and provide a quote.

kids.a: Yes. Our alpacas are socialized and gentle. All interactions are supervised by a handler. We advise children to approach calmly and follow the handler's guidance.

cancellation.q: What is your cancellation policy for weddings?
cancellation.a: Cancellation terms depend on the package. Please contact us for the specific policy for your booking. We aim to be as flexible as possible given the nature of special events.

weddings.subtitleLive: Alpaca weddings and photoshoots have been a US trend for years — now available in Europe. As the first and only alpaca farm on Ibiza, we offer unique wedding experiences among our 14 alpacas.

facts.title: Workshop at a Glance

san.title: About San
san.body: San is the weaver behind Wishfulfilling Weaving — the artisan studio at the heart of Es Currals alpaca farm. She works on a traditional wooden loom, turning fleece from our own herd into exclusive handcrafted textiles. The workshop is her invitation to share that craft with guests who want to go beyond watching and actually make something.

booking.title: How to Book
booking.body: The workshop runs off-season, when the farm is quieter and San has time to give you her full attention. There is no fixed calendar — send us a message with your preferred dates and we will confirm availability.

experience.a: None at all. The workshop is designed for complete beginners. San takes you through every step, from washing the raw fleece to finishing your scarf.

bring.a: Just yourself and comfortable clothes you do not mind getting a little dusty. All materials, tools, and equipment are provided. Lunch arrangements will be confirmed when you book.

cancellation.a: If you need to cancel or reschedule, please contact us as early as possible. Because workshops are scheduled on request and San sets aside two full days, we ask for reasonable notice.

wool.q: Is the wool from your own alpacas?
wool.a: Yes. You will work with fleece from our own herd at Es Currals — the same animals you can meet on a farm visit. The connection between the animal and the finished cloth is real.

sustainability.title: Sustainability
sustainability.subtitle: How we live and work on the land at Es Currals — animal welfare, traditional craft, and low-impact farming.
sustainability.welfareBody: The health and quality of life of our alpacas is the most important thing to us — full stop. Alpacas are popular and irresistibly charming animals, but as a sustainable eco-business we make it a point to keep the impact on both our animals and their natural environment as minimal as possible. Es Currals is a private family business, not a zoo or a circus. Our alpacas are not performing animals — they are individuals. Visits are by appointment only, precisely to keep stress on the herd to a minimum. OWNER_REVIEW_TRANSLATION
sustainability.craftBody: Alpacas are sheared only once a year, so every lock of fleece is almost literally worth its weight in gold. San processes all of it by hand in the Wishfulfilling Weaving studio: hand-washing the raw fleece, carding it, spinning the yarn, and weaving on Big Ben — a traditional Swedish wooden loom. She works from centuries-old patterns found in historical manuscripts, combining them with contemporary design. Every piece is unique and non-duplicable, made to order, 100% sustainable. OWNER_REVIEW_TRANSLATION
sustainability.dyesBody: The Wishfulfilling Weaving studio uses local flora to colour the wool through traditional methods. Hibiscus, avocado, and other plant and flower extracts give the palette its warmth. No synthetic chemical dyes and no machine processing — every colour comes directly from nature. The goal is to revive Ibiza's historical textile traditions through hands-on education in wool processing and natural dyeing. OWNER_REVIEW_TRANSLATION
sustainability.wasteBody: Nothing from the alpacas is wasted. Fleece that does not go into weaving is put back into the land through Alcaca Oro Negro — our branded alpaca manure fertilizer. Alpacas produce the purest, most fertile manure of any livestock species: small, odorless black pellets known in Peru as 'Oro Negro' (Black Gold). Bart manually filters every batch to remove stones, weeds and sand. Ready to use straight away — no composting needed — and effective for months to years. OWNER_REVIEW_TRANSLATION
sustainability.landBody: [UNMAPPED: confirm finca size in hectares before publishing] Es Currals is an authentic Ibicenco finca in the rural north of the island, surrounded by wild nature. The alpacas graze naturally; their manure replenishes the soil without artificial fertilizers or pesticides.
sustainability.sourcingBody: When San needs materials beyond our own fleece — linen, mohair, silk for certain commissions — she sources from suppliers who share the farm's values. Every creation is 100% natural materials, designed for lasting durability. Nothing is cut-price; nothing is cut-corner. OWNER_REVIEW_TRANSLATION

weaving.title: Wishfulfilling Weaving — Studio at Es Currals
weaving.subhead: Handwoven scarves from our herd's fleece. Traditional wooden loom. Slow craft, mostly alpaca, made on the farm.
weaving.processStep1Body: Each spring the alpacas are hand-shorn at Es Currals. The soft fleece is carefully stored per animal.
weaving.processStep2Body: San washes and cards the fleece by hand. No industrial process — pure craftsmanship.
weaving.processStep3Body: The yarn is spun and dyed with natural plant extracts — hibiscus, avocado, and other flowers.
weaving.processStep4Body: San weaves on Big Ben, a traditional Swedish wooden loom, using centuries-old patterns from historical manuscripts combined with contemporary fashion.
weaving.studioHistoryBody: San fell in love with weaving in 2013. She started on small table looms, then invested in a traditional Swedish wooden loom from a 92-year-old master weaver who gave her private lessons and named the loom Big Ben. Every step from shearing to finished cloth is done by hand on Es Currals. Softer than silk, rarer than cashmere, warmer than sheep's wool — and hypoallergenic.
